about: CHAIN saga_rhineland_flanders (Design/content/chains/saga_rhineland_flanders.md): GATES, BARS AND LOCKS. The saga of the Rhineland and Flanders is the five years in which the great army came off the sea and up the rivers: the winter camp in Saint Bavo's at Ganda (November 879), the wasted Scheldt (880), Colonia burned and its clergy fled to Mogontia with the saints' bodies (winter 881-882), the potters' earthquake and Archbishop Liutbert's wall and ditch (881-882), Colonia rebuilt 'with gates, bars and locks' (883), and the winter the Northmen sat in Diusburg while Duke Henry let them take no plunder (883-884). Sources: Annales Vedastini 879-881, Anglo-Saxon Chronicle 880, Annales Fuldenses 881-883, Regino of Pruem 884, as read in Design/content/dossiers (ganda, andoverpis, colonia, mogontia, diusburg) and chronicle_793.json; our own rendering, no modern translation quoted. No other chain tells these years. Fourteen cards, November 879 to 884 (the epilogue to 890). People met in more than one port (all invented, names of attested parts): Erminburg the ale-wife (Ganda, then Andoverpis), her man Odalbert the shipwright (taken at Ganda, found at Diusburg, home at Andoverpis), Soti the Dane who sells the army's takings (Ganda, then Diusburg and the Scheldt), Gozbert the keeper of Saint Peter's (Colonia, Mogontia, Colonia), the Frisian brothers Eilbod (Mogontia) and Eilward (Diusburg). Real: Duke Henry (died 28 August 886), Archbishop Liutbert of Mogontia (863-889), named in lines; Godfrid, the emperor Charles. Four endings: ch_saga_rhineland_flanders_end_held (history changed: Diusburg is not taken; flag changed_diusburg_883), _end_henry (what really happened: the duke's carrier), _end_wolf (the fort's trader), _end_after (the burnt well). A second change of history lies in the middle: flag changed_cologne_881 (Colonia shuts new gates in the winter of 881-882 and is not burned). Progress: every step sets its own flag ch_saga_rhineland_flanders_1 to _9 and _14; the flag _on means the saga has begun; branch flags are named in each note; every ending sets _done. Steps 1, 2, 3, 5 and 6 are each a way in (a house that trades only on the Rhine meets the saga at Colonia, Mogontia or Diusburg): they are roads, not gates, drawn at their port in their true months with a high weight, so a step missed in its year never stops the chain. Waits are real: the true dates, and the flag _wait set 'for' a number of days. No card is scheduled. Each option's note names its outcome text (chain_saga_rhineland_flanders.sNN.out_<option>) in Data/writing/chain_saga_rhineland_flanders.json. Written 6 Oct 2026. A draft for the user to overwrite.

cards.note: Step 1, a way in (drawn at Ganda from November 879 to October 880). The army from Fulham winters 'in Gandao monasterio' from November 879 (Annales Vedastini 879); it 'went from Fulham over sea to Ghent in Frankland, and sat there a year' (Anglo-Saxon Chronicle 880, Ingram 1823); chronicle_793.json 879-11-ghent-army. Saint Bavo's community had fled with the relics (dossiers/ganda.md 5; whether in 851 or 879 is not settled (?)). A man of the portus carried off by Northmen is in the Miracles of Bavo (dossiers/ganda.md 3: to Rouen, undated); shipwrights on this bank are in the annals for 811. Ours: that the camp sold its takings on the bank, Soti the dealer (invented; Soti is an attested Danish name), Erminburg the ale-wife (invented; Ermin- and -burg are attested Frankish name parts) and her man Odalbert the wright (invented; Odal- and -bert). Sets ch_saga_rhineland_flanders_1 and _on; then _bought_loot, or _carried.

cards.note: Step 2, a way in (drawn at Andoverpis from December 879 to October 881). In 880 the army wastes Tournai and every monastery on the Scheldt, moves to Courtrai in November 880, and after its defeat at Saucourt (3 August 881) comes back to Ganda to refit its ships before going to the Maas (Annales Vedastini 880, 881; dossiers/ganda.md 5; chronicle_793.json 881-08-03-saucourt). Andoverpis in these years is close-set timber houses on sill beams at the werf, with antler-comb makers, and no rampart yet (dossiers/andoverpis.md 2 and 4, after Bellens 2021); its church is Saint Peter and Saint Paul's (charter of 726). Ours: that refugees came down to the werf, the ransom chest, the boy out of the camp, and the priest Bertwin (invented; Bert- and -win). Erminburg is step 1's ale-wife. Sets ch_saga_rhineland_flanders_2 and _on; then _letter, _alms.

cards.note: Step 3, a way in (drawn at Colonia from August to December 881). In November 881 the army makes its camp at Elsloo on the Maas; in the winter it burns Colonia and Bonn 'with churches and buildings', and 'those who could get away, canons and nuns, fled to Mogontia, carrying with them the treasures of the churches and the bodies of the saints' (Annales Fuldenses 881, our rendering; chronicle_793.json 881-winter-aachen-cologne). A ransom paid in January did not save the town (dossiers/colonia.md 5, after de.wikipedia 'Raubzuege der Wikinger in das Rheinland' (?)). In 883 it was rebuilt 'with gates, bars and locks' (AF 883), which is why this card has the gates of 881 without doors: that is ours, as are the argument in the porch, Gozbert the keeper (invented; Goz- and -bert) and Reginbald the wine shipper (invented; Regin- and -bald). The Roman wall: 3.9 km, nine gates, 8 m high (dossiers/colonia.md 1). The archbishop is Willibert (870-889), not shown. HISTORY CHANGED on the option 'gates' if it succeeds: flag changed_cologne_881 (the town shuts new doors and is passed by, as it really was in 883). Sets ch_saga_rhineland_flanders_3, _on and the wait; then _gates and changed_cologne_881, or _ransom_paid, or _saints.

cards.note: Step 4 (drawn at Mogontia from February to September 882, after step 3). 'On the third day before the Kalends of January, before cockcrow, there was an earthquake at Mogontia ... earthen vessels, as the potters bore witness, were knocked against each other and broken' (Annales Fuldenses 881, our rendering: 30 December 881). The clergy of Colonia and Bonn are in the town with the treasures and the saints' bodies (AF 881). The king's chapel at Aachen used as a stable: AF 881. Saint Alban's on the hill south of the wall is where the great are buried (dossiers/mogontia.md 2); that Colonia's saints were lodged there is ours. Gozbert is step 3's keeper; the potter is unnamed. The pay of the middle of the chain (a Turn): the freight, or a place in Saint Peter's prayers with the key riddle and Latin lessons. Sets ch_saga_rhineland_flanders_4 and the wait; then _remembered.

cards.note: Step 5, a way in (drawn at Mogontia from May 882 to June 883). In 882, the Northmen having burned as far as Koblenz, the repair of Mogontia's wall was begun and a ditch dug outside it (Annales Fuldenses 882; dossiers/mogontia.md 2); the archbishop is Liutbert (863-889), named, not shown. The Frisians' shore: long plots from the wall to jetties; 'the best part of the city, where the Frisians lived' (AF 886, when it burned). In July 882 the emperor Charles besieged the camp on the Maas for twelve days and then made terms: Godfrid was baptised and given Frisia, and silver was paid; Franks who had gone into the fort 'some to trade, some to look at the works' were shut in when the Northmen closed the gate, and were killed or kept in irons for ransom (AF 882, our rendering; chronicle_793.json 882-07-asselt-godfrid). This is the warning for step 8's danger. Ours: the Frisian brothers Eilbod of Mogontia and Eilward of Diusburg (invented; Eil-, -bod and -ward are attested Frisian name parts), and the steward's order. Frisians at Diusburg are first written of in 893 (the Pruem estate book), the market there is dug from about 870-880 (dossiers/diusburg.md). Sets ch_saga_rhineland_flanders_5 and _on; then _word, _wall.

cards.note: Step 6, a way in (drawn at Diusburg from March to October 883). The place: the king's court on a flood-free hill, unfortified in the ninth century, a market at its foot in use from about 870-880, a timber well tree-ring dated to 872, and Frisians who 'stay' there (written 893) (dossiers/diusburg.md 1 and 2, after Krause). 'Northmen who had come from Denmark to Kennemerland went up the Rhine by ship with Godfrid's consent' (Regino of Pruem, year 884, our rendering). Colonia has its new gates in 883 (AF 883). Ours: Eilward (step 5), his cloth and his children, the king's steward and his eleven men, and the bank: the digs found no rampart before the tenth century, so a bank staked across the neck of the hill in 883 is the player's doing and part of a changed history (step 10). Sets ch_saga_rhineland_flanders_6 and _on; then _moved, _bank, or _bought_cheap.

cards.note: Step 7 (drawn at Colonia from June to November 883, once the saga has begun). 'Colonia Agrippina was rebuilt, without its churches and monasteries, and its walls were restored with gates, bars and locks' (Annales Fuldenses 883, our rendering). The same year 'the Northmen, coming up the bed of the Rhine, burned many places lately restored and took no small plunder; Liutbert, archbishop of Mogontia, met them with a few men, struck down not a few of them and shook the plunder out of them' (AF 883, our rendering). Duke Henry is the Henry who camps against the Northmen at Diusburg that winter (Regino 884); his buyer is invented and unnamed. Ours: that Henry's man bought stores at Colonia, and that a merchant's word could bring spears to Diusburg a month early: with step 6's bank that is the changed history of step 10. Gozbert is step 3's keeper. Sets ch_saga_rhineland_flanders_7; then _henry_early, or _victualler.

cards.note: Step 8 (drawn at Diusburg from November 883 to March 884, once the saga has begun, unless the bank was dug and the duke warned: then step 10 comes instead). 'Occupying the town of Diusburh they built a fortification in that place in their usual way and stayed in it the whole winter. Duke Henry set his camp against them and allowed them to take no plunder' (Regino of Pruem, year 884, our rendering). Henry's camp is put at Broich, at the Hellweg's crossing of the Ruhr, by Krause (dossiers/diusburg.md 2). The burn layer across the settlement and what Krause reads as the plunder of the Frisians: dossiers/diusburg.md 2 and 8. THE DANGER IS WARNED: step 5 told of the traders shut inside the fort on the Maas (AF 882), and Eilward says it again here; the option 'fort' is a chance and its label says so. Soti is step 1's Dane; that he came on to the Rhine with this fleet is ours, as is all trade at the fort. Duke Henry (historical; died 28 August 886 before Paris) is shown at his camp. Sets ch_saga_rhineland_flanders_8 and the wait; then _fed (to the ending _end_henry), _fort (to _end_wolf), or _away (to _end_after).

cards.note: Step 9 (drawn at Diusburg from December 883 to March 884, ten days or more after step 8, unless the boat turned away). Two ship rivets of northern kind, 7 cm long, were found in the burn layer at Diusburg (dossiers/diusburg.md 2, after Krause): ships were mended there. The army refitted its ships at Ganda in 881 (Annales Vedastini 881). Ours: Odalbert (step 1's wright), four winters a captive, the ransom and the rescue. A skilled captive's ransom at 120 d is two and a half times the game's price of a captive (goods_793.json: 48 d). The night rescue is a chance and the line before it says how the ships are watched. Sets ch_saga_rhineland_flanders_9; then _wright, or _wright_word.

cards.note: ENDING 1, _end_held: HISTORY CHANGED (drawn at Diusburg from November 883 to the end of 886, when step 6's bank was dug and step 7's word reached the duke). What really happened is step 8: the Northmen occupied the town, fortified it and wintered there (Regino 884). Here the hill is held before they come, and they go back down the river: flag changed_diusburg_883. What would follow is on the chain's page: no burn layer, no hasty graves, the well of 872 clean, the Frisians of the 893 estate book richer and earlier, and perhaps a later palace, since the planned rebuilding after 883-884 was a rebuilding of what had burned (dossiers/diusburg.md 2). The hardest road, so it pays most and gives two grand rewards: a plot at Diusburg (Frisians held house ground there under Pruem by 893) and a sworn partner in Eilward (partnerships between merchants who 'stay' in one settlement and trade from another are the pattern of the Frisian houses at Mogontia, Colonia and Diusburg; ours). Odalbert swimming ashore is ours. Sets ch_saga_rhineland_flanders_end_held, changed_diusburg_883, _wright and _done.

cards.title: The hill that was held
cards.intention: The ships came up with the first frost. They looked at the ditch, the stakes and the duke's spears along the bank, lay one night on the far shore among the old Roman stones, and went back down with the stream.

cards.note: ENDING 2, _end_henry: WHAT REALLY HAPPENED (drawn at Diusburg or Colonia from April 884 to June 886, for the house that fed or ferried for the duke in step 8). 'When spring came back they burned their camp and made for the places by the sea' (Regino of Pruem, year 884, our rendering). Burnt house walls across the whole settlement, a timber well filled with burnt rubble, and hasty burials, one of a man about two metres tall: Krause's digs, and his reading that they belong to that winter (dossiers/diusburg.md 2 and 8 (?)). Clamps that held moss caulking between planks are found at Diusburg from the ninth century (dossiers/diusburg.md 4): hence the caulkers' gift, ship_upgrades_793.json moss_laths. The grand reward is a lord's protection: Henry was the emperor's chief commander against the Northmen from 884 to his death before Paris on 28 August 886, when it lapses. The hard road (the Frisians carried to Colonia, or Colonia's gates, or its saints) adds a factor at Diusburg. Sets ch_saga_rhineland_flanders_end_henry and _done.

cards.note: ENDING 3, _end_wolf (drawn at Diusburg from March to June 884, or at Andoverpis from May 884 to the end of 885, for the house that traded at the fort in step 8). The Northmen burn their camp in spring and go back to the coast (Regino 884). Ours: all of it. What it rests on: the Norse felag, the laying of goods together by sworn partners (the word is on rune stones of about 1000, Sigtuna and elsewhere (?)); raiders who traded what they took (the camp markets of the great army in England; Rimbert on Birka's Danes (?)); and the Frankish bans on selling to the Northmen, which is why this ending carries a cost that lasts: the flag ch_saga_rhineland_flanders_wolf_mark (the duke's men and the Frisians of the Rhine remember the boat), unless the cloth is given back. Sets ch_saga_rhineland_flanders_end_wolf and _done.

cards.note: ENDING 4, _end_after (drawn at Diusburg from April 884 to the end of 886 for any house in the saga that neither fed the duke nor traded at the fort: it turned away, or was elsewhere that winter). History as it was: the camp burned in spring 884 (Regino 884); burnt walls across the settlement and the timber well of 872 filled with burnt rubble; two ship rivets of northern kind, 7 cm long (dossiers/diusburg.md 2, after Krause); caulking clamps (the same, 4). Wine kept in a pit under the floor is ours, from the cellared houses of the later palace ring. Eilbod's purse is ours: the richer brother up the river sets the other up again, as the Frisian houses of Mogontia and Diusburg are one trade in two places. Every option is worth 600 d or more and gives a grand reward: a factor, or a plot. Sets ch_saga_rhineland_flanders_end_after and _done.

cards.note: Step 14, the epilogue (drawn at Andoverpis to the end of 890, once the wright is free or the saga has ended; not an ending: it closes the Scheldt people's story whatever the ending was). Houses on sill beams, close set, some of reused ship's timber: Andoverpis in the later ninth century (dossiers/andoverpis.md 2, after Bellens and Van de Walle). Ships were built on the Scheldt at Ganda in 811 and refitted there in 881 (Annales regni Francorum 811; Annales Vedastini 881). Towing gear for the rivers: boats are hauled up the Rhine by a rope from the bank 'as the custom is' (Wandalbert, Miracula sancti Goaris, 839; dossiers/mogontia.md 1); ship_upgrades_793.json tow_gear. The riddle is the Exeter Book's mead (riddles_793.json riddle_exeter_27_mead), given as the ale-wife's own. Ours: all the people. Sets ch_saga_rhineland_flanders_14.
